Engineering Manager, Hardware Design - Path Robotics | Built In

At Path Robotics, we’re not just solving a manufacturing challenge. We’re solving a recruiting problem.

The Role

Lead and develop a mechanical engineering team designing robotic hardware, sensing end-of-arm tooling, fixtures, and electromechanical systems. Own technical strategy, resource planning, design reviews, cross-functional integration, prototyping, testing, validation, production release, and deployment. Partner with robotics, software, ML, electrical engineering, suppliers, and manufacturing teams to deliver reliable hardware and resolve field issues.

Build the Path Forward

At Path Robotics, we’re building the future of embodied intelligence. Our AI-driven systems enable robots to adapt, learn, and perform in the real world closing the skilled labor gap and transforming industries. We go beyond traditional methods, combining perception, reasoning, and control to deliver field-ready AI that is risk-aware, reliable, and continuously improving through real-world use.

Big, hard problems are our everyday work, and our team of intelligent, humble, and driven people make the impossible possible together.

We're looking for an experienced Engineering Manager, Mechanical Engineering & Hardware Design to lead the design and development of mechanical systems supporting Path's next generation of robotic manipulation products as we expand into factory automation.

As part of our Sensing and Embodied Intelligence team, you'll lead a team of engineers responsible for sensing end-of-arm tooling, robotic hardware, and the physical interfaces connecting robots, sensors, tools, and workpieces.

This is a hands-on leadership role that combines deep mechanical engineering expertise with people management, technical strategy, and cross-functional execution. You'll help define engineering direction, develop high-performing teams, and deliver reliable, scalable hardware solutions from concept through deployment.

What You’ll Do

* Lead, mentor, and develop a team of mechanical engineers, providing technical guidance, performance feedback, and career development.
* Own engineering priorities, resource planning, and execution of mechanical hardware development initiatives.
* Oversee the design and development of sensing end-of-arm tooling, robotic components, fixtures, and electromechanical systems.
* Drive the integration of cameras, 3D sensors, force/torque sensors, tactile sensors, and other sensing technologies into robotic hardware.
* Define mechanical and physical interfaces between robots, tools, sensors, fixtures, and workpieces.
* Lead technical design reviews and establish standards for reliability, manufacturability, serviceability, and system performance.
* Partner with ML, Robotics, Software, and Electrical Engineering teams to translate product and model training requirements into hardware solutions.
* Support the design of tasks, fixtures, and environments used to collect robotic manipulation training data.
* Oversee the full hardware development lifecycle, including requirements, prototyping, testing, validation, production release, and deployment.
* Work closely with vendors, suppliers, and internal manufacturing teams to accelerate hardware development.
* Drive root-cause analysis, continuous improvement, and resolution of technical challenges identified during testing and field deployment.
* Support hiring, team development, and the establishment of scalable engineering processes as Path grows.

Who You Are

* Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Robotics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
* 7+ years of experience in mechanical engineering, robotics, automation, or industrial hardware development.
* 2+ years of experience leading or managing engineering teams.
* Strong technical background in mechanical design, electromechanical systems, and robotic hardware development.
* Experience designing end-of-arm tooling, grippers, fixtures, or sensor-integrated robotic systems.
* Understanding of sensor integration, calibration, mechanical tolerances, and hardware reliability.
* Experience developing mechanical and electrical interfaces for complex robotic systems.
* Proficiency in SolidWorks or equivalent CAD software and PDM-based design workflows.
* Demonstrated success bringing complex hardware products from concept through production and deployment.
* Strong technical judgment, project management skills, and ability to balance competing engineering priorities.
* Passionate about developing engineers, solving complex technical challenges, and building high-performing teams.

Chief Engineer, Manufacturing Excellence at Nextpower — Mesa, AZ | LinkedIn Jobs

Job Description Location: Mesa, Arizona; hybrid as business needs require

Employment type: Full-time

Position Overview

The Chief Engineer, Manufacturing Excellence sets the technical direction and standards for manufacturing across Nextpower facilities and contract manufacturing partners. This role turns product, customer, and business needs into manufacturing processes that are safe, reliable, high quality, cost-effective, and ready to scale.

As a recognized technical expert, you’ll lead complex, high-impact initiatives across manufacturing, engineering, quality, reliability, supply chain, IT, and operations. You’ll guide product launches and factory readiness, strengthen manufacturing capability across sites, and help shape the organization’s long-term approach to manufacturing excellence.

Key Responsibilities

* Set the technical strategy, standards, and governance for manufacturing processes across internal facilities and contract manufacturers.
* Lead multi-site efforts to standardize processes, work instructions, control plans, quality checks, performance measures, and continuous improvement practices.
* Guide design-for-manufacturability and design-for-test reviews, helping teams address production risks early in product development.
* Establish manufacturing process architecture, critical-to-quality characteristics, standard work, and control plans.
* Set expectations for process capability, PFMEA, statistical process control (SPC), APQP, process validation, and production readiness.
* Provide technical direction for factory readiness, pilot builds, production launches, ramp-up, and ongoing improvement programs.
* Lead improvements in first-pass yield, throughput, cycle time, manufacturing cost, and defect reduction.
* Guide the development and use of automation, tooling, fixtures, end-of-line testing, and manufacturing data systems.
* Lead resolution of significant manufacturing problems using root-cause analysis, 8D, and other structured problem-solving methods.
* Establish technical capability and quality expectations for contract manufacturers and strategic suppliers; review their performance and improvement plans.
* Coordinate engineering and process changes with Engineering, Quality, Reliability, Supply Chain, IT, Operations, and manufacturing partners.
* Review manufacturing KPIs, process capability data, audit findings, nonconformance reports, corrective actions, and reliability trends to identify business-wide risks and opportunities.
* Provide technical leadership and mentorship to manufacturing engineers; build organizational capability in Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma.
* Help ensure manufacturing processes meet applicable safety, quality, regulatory, and customer requirements.
* Communicate complex technical recommendations clearly and influence decisions across teams, sites, suppliers, and leadership.

Required Qualifications

* Bachelor’s degree in Manufacturing, Mechanical, Electrical, Industrial, or Systems Engineering, or a related technical field; equivalent experience may be considered.
* Typically, 12 or more years of related experience with a bachelor’s degree, 8 or more years with a master’s degree, or 5 or more years with a PhD.
* Extensive manufacturing engineering, manufacturing excellence, or operations engineering experience, including leadership of large-scale process development and improvement.
* Experience with power electronics, high-voltage products, inverters, energy systems, or similarly complex electromechanical products.
* Advanced knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, SPC, PFMEA, APQP, process validation, and process capability analysis.
* Demonstrated success leading factory readiness, product launches, production ramp-up, and continuous improvement across multiple sites or manufacturing partners.
* Experience setting technical requirements and managing manufacturing relationships with contract manufacturers and strategic suppliers.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing test systems, traceability, MES or ERP data, and production performance reporting.
* Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary initiatives and influence decisions across engineering, quality, operations, supply chain, and supplier teams.
* Excellent technical communication, problem-solving, and program leadership skills.

Preferred Qualifications

* Master’s degree in a relevant engineering or technical discipline.
* Experience establishing manufacturing standards, governance, or operating models across a global or multi-site organization.
* Experience with automation strategy, factory digitalization, or manufacturing data systems.
* Relevant certifications in Lean, Six Sigma, quality, or project leadership.
